Hi Maria —

Thanks for the files, this is a great start. Quick responses below and I added Vanessa and Kim to align on marketplace copy and imagery. Ben, looping you for any AMI/SKU operational constraints.

SKU strategy (quick take):
- For buyer experience and co-sell attribution, we recommend separate SKUs per tier with a clear Starter->Pro upgrade path. It simplifies procurement and reporting.
- Use usage-based metering for add-on compute (if applicable) but surface a per-hour or monthly list price for each SKU so enterprise procurement has a tangible line item.

Hero image: I’ll defer to Vanessa on creative but initial preference is variant B (clean product screenshot + customer callout) — it signals product maturity.

CTA wording: From a co-sell motion perspective, “Request demo” maps well to sales-led opportunities, while “Start free trial” tends to work for PLG-first teams. If Acme wants AWS attribution and co-sell leads, I’d recommend default CTA = “Request demo” and secondary CTA = “Start free trial” (if you can support both).

Next steps:
- Vanessa: can you review attachments and suggest a hero final?
- Ben: confirm if separate SKUs create AMI/AMI-tagging or metering work for Acme.
- Maria: any constraints from Acme on having both CTAs visible?

Priya
Head of GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priya & Maria — I reviewed the attached blurb doc and hero options. A few concrete, prioritized suggestions for marketplace listing performance and co-sell clarity: 

Hero + imagery
- Variant A (abstract cloud shape) is too generic for category differentiation.
- Variant B (screenshot + 3-line customer quote) wins for discovery. Use a cropped screenshot that highlights inference latency dashboard; place a small badge "Redwood-verified performance" on the lower-right.
- Provide a 1:1.91 hero and a 1:1 square for thumbnails — AWS will require both.

Headline + subhead (one-liners that perform)
- Headline (short): "Low-latency LLM inference — predictable cost and scale"
- Subhead (expand): "Run LLM inference on your terms: hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, or private deployments. Optimized for throughput and cost."

CTA strategy (recommendation)
- Primary CTA: "Request demo" (for co-sell + lead capture).
- Secondary CTA: "Start free trial" (PLG-oriented buyers — only show if Acme can enable an AWS-trial flow).
- Backup microcopy: below CTA, a one-line note: "AWS Marketplace purchase and billing available" to reduce procurement friction.

SKU bundling + marketplace labels
- Keep three SKUs but align SKU IDs and descriptions to match the AMI tags: ACME-Redwood-Starter, ACME-Redwood-Pro, ACME-Redwood-Enterprise. Make sure the SKU table in Excel maps each SKU to the AMI ID, pricing unit (hourly vs. monthly), and included support level.

Telemetry & co-sell handshake
- Add a field in the product listing notes: "Sales contact for co-sell: partnerships@acmeai.com" and include the HubSpot ID in the listing assets so AWS can attach co-sell attribution.

I attached a quick copy doc with my edits (I pasted the hero/headline options at the top of marketing_blurbs.docx).

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Growth PM, Marketplace & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
